correctness.rationale: For the exact ordinary 3-cut definition, the 12 cube edges form the 4-regular 24-edge cuboctahedral line graph. Independent exhaustive reconstruction finds 164 disconnected induced triples and 164 complements of size 9, giving nonempty f=(12,66,220,495,792,924,792,489,164), 3954 faces and 23208 Hasse covers. The specified vertex-stage matching has 1968 pairs, 18 critical faces in dimensions 0:1, 7:6, 8:11, and a complete 3954-node topological sort verifies no directed Morse cycles. Independently programmed signed recursive elimination gives exactly the stated 6x11 integer Morse differential, of rational rank 5 with determinant -1 for the asserted 5x5 minor. Therefore coker(d8)=Z and ker(d8)=Z^6 (no torsion), and all other positive cellular groups vanish. The CW 7-skeleton is wedge^6 S7 and all maps S7 -> wedge^6 S7 are classified by Z^6 degree vectors; unimodular changes of basis cancel five unit-degree 7/8 pairs, giving S7 vee six S8. Pure dimension 8 with H7 nonzero contradicts pure shellability. Independent original-face mod-2 ranks (11,55,165,330,462,462,330,158) corroborate but are not used as an integral proof. Exact scope is one graph, not an infinite family.
residual_risks: The independent exhaustive finite computation is for this single 12-vertex graph and does not prove a larger cube-line-graph family.
Morse signed elimination relies on the acyclic matching and degree classification; these hypotheses were independently checked, not assumed from a VERIFY_OK log.
No Lean proof or expert attestation is supplied; finite arithmetic plus standard topology establish only the stated natural-object result.

evidence: Bayer et al. Theorem 6.1 requires the complete (n-k-2)=7 skeleton; the candidate has exactly 489 rather than C(12,8)=495 eight-vertex faces, so the theorem cannot establish its torsion-freeness or sphere wedge.

Bayer et al. II Proposition 2.17 gives a conditional Euler-characteristic formula using the missing complements of connected triples and 4-cycles. Here the 56 connected triples and exactly six cycle quadruples yield reduced Euler characteristic 55+6-56=5 if the stated face-lattice criterion is applied; this is not enough to recover the two Betti ranks or the homotopy equivalence.
Published short-cycle-free results require absence of 4-cycles; L(Q_3) contains six four-cycles, as exact independent enumeration establishes.
Chandrakar et al. arXiv:2408.07646, Theorems 1.1 and 1.2: rectangular 2xn,3xn grid families, not the 4-regular twelve-vertex line graph L(Q_3).

No inspected stronger theorem determines the integral (1,6) adjacent Betti ranks and wedge homotopy.

value.rationale: The cuboctahedron L(Q3) is a canonical twelve-vertex vertex-transitive Archimedean/polyhedral and line-graph object, and ordinary 3-cut topology is a motivated established invariant. The exact integral mixed-dimensional wedge type is not inferred from the prior Euler count, known cube case or strong full-skeleton theorem (which is obstructed by six square complements). It determines both positive-dimensional integral homology ranks, excludes torsion, and certifies nonshellability in a pure eight-complex; these precise homotopy invariants can be used to compare other polyhedral/line-graph cut complexes and test extensions of the face-lattice theory. The result is a natural finite exact classification with a sharp structural boundary, not a claim of a general theorem.
residual_risks: A single finite graph classification does not imply a uniform formula for all cubical line graphs and makes no equivariant module claim.

Euler characteristic 5 is accessible from earlier general face-lattice methods; value lies in splitting adjacent integral Betti ranks, torsion elimination and homotopy/non-shellability, not a novel Euler count.

final_claim: For the 12-vertex cuboctahedral graph C=L(Q3), with ordinary Delta_3(C) generated by complements of disconnected induced triples, Delta_3(C) is homotopy equivalent to S^7 vee 6 S^8. Integral reduced homology is Z at degree 7 and Z^6 at degree 8, and vanishes otherwise. The pure eight-dimensional complex is nonshellable, and its f-vector is (12,66,220,495,792,924,792,489,164).
limitations: Only the ordinary 3-cut complex of the specified 12-vertex graph is proved; no assertion for all line graphs of hypercubes or their symmetry representations.

The published icosahedral 3-cut complex has the same homotopy formula for a different graph, and prior literature already implies some combinatorial/Euler information; the assessed new fact is this graph-specific integral wedge classification.
